chunks.text: The primary palette is Acme Red (#C8102E) with charcoal text. Use red sparingly: buttons and key highlights only.
Headings use Inter Bold; body copy uses Source Serif at 18 px with a line height of 1.6.
Keep clear space around the logo equal to the height of the A. Never stretch, recolour or rotate the mark.
Photos show real staff in natural light. Avoid stock images of handshakes or people pointing at laptops.
Releases go out from the main branch through the pipeline. Tag the commit, wait for the green build, then promote the staging image to production.
If errors spike after a release, redeploy the previous image tag from the pipeline history. The database migrations are additive, so the old code keeps working.
No releases on Friday afternoons or during the two weeks before a product launch, unless the client signs off.
The database is backed up every night and kept for thirty days. A restore drill runs on the first Monday of each month.
User passwords are hashed with Argon2id and a per-user salt; plain text is never stored or logged.
Every staff account must enrol an authenticator app. SMS codes are not accepted for admin accounts.
Each quarter the project lead reviews who can reach the hosting dashboard and removes anyone who has left.
Report a suspected breach to the security channel within one hour. Do not try to clean up evidence yourself.
Senior designer: 120 per hour. Developer: 110 per hour. Project manager: 95 per hour.
Retainers of more than forty hours a month get ten percent off the hourly rates.
Invoices are due within thirty days. Late payments accrue two percent interest per month.
Travel outside the city is billed at cost with receipts; mileage at the government rate.
Acme wants more demo requests from the website: the target is fifty qualified leads a month by the end of the year.
Discovery runs for two weeks, design for four, build for six. Launch is planned for the first week of November.
The product team may change pricing tiers mid-project, which would mean rewriting the pricing page late.
Dana from marketing approves copy; Lee from engineering approves anything touching the signup flow.
Write plainly and warmly. Prefer short sentences and active verbs; avoid jargon such as synergy or leverage.
Headlines use sentence case, stay under sixty characters and lead with the benefit to the reader.
Spell out numbers one to nine; use numerals from 10. Dates are written as 4 March 2026.
Link text says where it goes. Never use click here or read more on its own.
Target phrases are inventory software for small warehouses and stock control app, mapped one page each.
Every old URL gets a permanent 301 redirect to its closest new page; the mapping lives in the redirects spreadsheet.
The sitemap is generated at build time and submitted to Search Console after launch.
Each page has a unique meta description of about 150 characters that matches the page heading.
Track demo_request_submitted, pricing_viewed and signup_started as custom events with the plan name attached.
No tracking script loads until the visitor accepts the cookie banner; declining keeps only the essential cookie.
A weekly dashboard shows visits, demo requests and conversion rate by traffic source.
The work covers twelve page templates, the blog, the pricing page and integration with the existing CRM.
Anything outside scope needs a written change request with a price and a new date before work starts.
The client has five working days to review each deliverable; silence after that counts as approval.
Copyright in the final designs passes to Acme once the last invoice is paid in full.
Grey placeholder text on white fails WCAG AA at 2.9 to 1; darken it to at least 4.5 to 1.
The mega menu cannot be opened with the keyboard and focus is invisible on the search button.
Icons without labels are announced as unlabelled button; add an aria-label to each.
Error messages appear only in red; also show an icon and text so colour is not the only signal.
Hero images are served as AVIF under 150 KB, with explicit width and height to stop layout shift.
Self-host two font files at most and preload only the body font.
Keep the initial JavaScript under 200 KB compressed; the chat widget loads only after the visitor scrolls.
Largest contentful paint stays under 2.5 seconds on a mid-range phone over 4G.
The newsletter goes out on the second Tuesday of every month at 9 in the morning.
Only people who opted in through the signup form are added; the old trade show list is not imported.
Every email has a one-click unsubscribe link, honoured within two days.
The domain is registered with the client's registrar; we manage DNS records through their account.
TLS certificates renew automatically every sixty days; an alert fires if one is within a week of expiry.
Static assets are cached at the edge for a year with hashed file names; HTML is cached for five minutes.
After launch we answer support tickets on weekdays from 9 to 5, Acme's local time.
Site-down issues get a reply within one hour; cosmetic bugs within three working days.
Two editor training sessions are included: one for publishing posts, one for updating the pricing table.
Full-time staff get twenty-five days of paid leave a year plus public holidays.
Book time off in the HR tool at least two weeks ahead and tell the project lead.
Up to five unused days carry over to the next year; the rest expire on 31 March.
Submit expense claims with a photo of the receipt by the fifth of the following month.
Meals while travelling are covered up to 40 per day; alcohol is never reimbursed.
Laptops and monitors are bought by the studio; ask before buying anything over 200.
On the first day a new starter gets their email, chat and password manager accounts.
Every new hire is paired with a buddy who answers questions during the first month.
In the first week they shadow a client call and ship one small fix to production.
Design work happens in Figma; shared components live in the studio library file.
Log hours daily in the time tracker against the client project; untracked time cannot be invoiced.
Client credentials are kept only in the shared vault, never in chat messages or documents.
Everyone is reachable between 10 and 3 so meetings fit in those hours.
The studio pays up to 300 once for a desk chair or headset for working from home.
The Beta mobile app needs offline sync for field technicians and a barcode scanner screen.
Beta's budget allows a senior designer for three weeks and two developers for ten.
